A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

F1651 phase‐switching is a two‐stage process, the first being the formation and dissociation of Lrp complexes at the F1651 promoter, followed by the binding of the Lrp–FooI complex to the F1651 activator sites.

the ON/OFF switch rate during F‐phase variation is dependent on the relative affinities of Lrp for its binding sites 1 to 3, and the relative affinity of Lrp for the activator binding sites is determined by FooI.

the stability of the Lrp–DNA complex is a major determinant of the ON cell level during phase variation.
